dayInLife.what: Breakfast at home, no commute, no packed lunch, no 7am panic.

faq.q: Is bina a homeschool program or a school?
faq.a: A school. Your child has a class, a timetable, certified teachers and report cards — the same structure as an in-person school, delivered live online. Most state programs list us under online or nonpublic schooling rather than homeschool curriculum, and we tell you exactly which category applies in your state before you apply.

faq.q: What if my state approves me for less than the full amount?
faq.a: You pay the difference. We show you the number before you commit, and we offer quarterly and yearly plans plus $1,500 off per additional child, so the gap is a monthly figure you can plan around.

faq.q: What if my application is turned down, or the window has closed?
faq.a: You are not stuck with a school you never chose. Families join bina and pay directly while an application is pending, and we time your start around your funding date once it is confirmed. Nothing about enrolling forces you to wait for the state.

faq.q: My child is neurodivergent or has an IEP. Does that change anything?
faq.a: Often in your favor — several states fund more per child for special needs. On our side, small classes and a Family Success team are the whole point; parents of neurodivergent children are a large share of our families, and they say so in the reviews on this page.

faq.q: Can I use ESA money for bina alongside other things?
faq.a: That depends on your state's rules and your award, not on us. Tuition for an online school is an approved category in the states listed here; whether there is room left over for other purchases is a question for your state's handbook, and we will point you at the exact page.

faq.q: Is bina an approved Arizona ESA school?
faq.a: Yes. bina has been an approved school on ClassWallet since November 2024, and the Arizona Department of Education confirmed our registration in June 2026.

faq.q: Does the ESA cover all of bina's tuition?
faq.a: It covers most of it. On the yearly plan, families usually top up about $231–$314 a month, depending on their award.

faq.q: Is there an application deadline?
faq.a: Arizona accepts applications all year. The date you sign your ESA agreement sets which quarter your funding starts, so applying earlier means funding starts sooner.

faq.q: How long does approval take?
faq.a: Up to 45 days after you apply, according to the Arizona Department of Education.

faq.q: How does bina get paid?
faq.a: We send you an invoice. You create an order in ClassWallet, the state reviews it and pays bina directly, usually within about a week.

faq.q: Can my child start before the ESA is approved?
faq.a: Yes. You can enroll and pay bina directly while your application is being reviewed, then switch to ESA funding once it's approved.

faq.q: Will someone help me with the application?
faq.a: Yes. Our financial aid team guides you through every step, from the application to your first payment.

faq.q: Do you offer a sibling discount?
faq.a: Yes. Each additional child gets $1,500 off tuition.

faq.q: My child is in public school now. Can we still apply?
faq.a: Yes. Your child can apply while in public school and studies with bina once your ESA is active.

faq.q: Is bina responsible for this program?
faq.a: The Empowerment Scholarship Account (ESA) is run by the state of Arizona, not by bina. Program amounts, eligibility and deadlines are subject to change. Always confirm with the official program site before you rely on a number here.

Your child is enrolled in, or eligible to enroll in, a West Virginia public school from kindergarten to grade 12. bina teaches from Pre-K to Grade 10. Pre-K isn't covered by the Hope Scholarship.
Your child is at least 5 before July 1.
From 2026–27, every West Virginia K–12 student can apply, including children already in private school or homeschool.
Your child isn't enrolled full time in a public school.

Applications are open all year, and the date you apply sets your first-year award. For 2026–27: 50% of the award until November 30, 2026, and 25% from December 1, 2026 to February 28, 2027. After February 28, applications count toward the 2027–28 school year.

howEsa.title: The Hope Scholarship in plain words
howEsa.body: The Hope Scholarship is West Virginia's Education Savings Account, run by the West Virginia State Treasurer's Office. When your child is approved and your Notice of Intent is on file, the state puts money into a Hope account for your child's education, a quarter of the award at a time (by August 15, October 15, January 15 and April 15). You spend it on approved expenses, including tuition at an online school like bina, and the money goes from your account to the school, not to you.

faq.q: Is bina approved for the Hope Scholarship?
faq.a: Yes. bina is approved for West Virginia's Hope Scholarship, so you can use your Hope funds toward bina tuition.

faq.q: Does the Hope Scholarship cover all of bina's tuition?
faq.a: It covers about half. With the full award, families on the yearly plan top up about $444 a month.

faq.q: When can I apply?
faq.a: Applications are open all year, and the date you apply sets your first-year award. If you apply by November 30, 2026, you receive 50% of the 2026–27 award, and from December 1, 2026 to February 28, 2027, you receive 25%. From the next school year, you receive the full award.

faq.q: What is a Notice of Intent?
faq.a: A form you file with your county board of education once your application shows "Eligible". You file it once, and your Hope account is funded only after it's on file.

faq.q: When does the money arrive?
faq.a: The state adds a quarter of the award to your account by August 15, October 15, January 15 and April 15.

faq.q: My child is in public school now. Can we still apply?
faq.a: Yes. Every West Virginia K–12 student can apply. Your child can't stay enrolled full time in a public school while using Hope funds, so they move to bina once you're ready to start.

faq.q: Is there anything I need to do each year?
faq.a: Yes. Confirm your child's place in the program between January 5 and June 15 each year. We send you new paperwork for it.

faq.q: Will someone help me with the application?
faq.a: Yes. Our financial aid team guides you through every step, from the application to your first payment.

faq.q: Do you offer a sibling discount?
faq.a: Yes. Each additional child gets $1,500 off tuition.

faq.q: Is bina responsible for this program?
faq.a: The Hope Scholarship is run by the state of West Virginia, not by bina. Program amounts, eligibility and deadlines are subject to change. Always confirm with the official program site before you rely on a number here.

howEsa.title: FES-UA in plain words
howEsa.body: FES-UA is a Florida education savings account for students with unique abilities, managed by Step Up For Students (SUFS). The state deposits money into an account each quarter, and families spend it on approved costs, including part-time tutoring.

bullets.v: depends on your child's grade, county and needs. Our financial aid team will go through your numbers with you.
unused funds roll over each year, up to a $50,000 account cap.
bina isn't paid directly from the account. You pay bina, then ask SUFS to reimburse you.

items.v: Your child lives in Florida.
At least 3 by December 31, 2026, and under 22 on September 1, 2026.

An IEP from a Florida school district, or a qualifying diagnosis from a licensed physician, physician assistant, APRN or psychologist (for example autism, ADHD, Down syndrome, or a speech or language impairment).
No income limit.
New 2026–27 applications close November 15, 2026.

covered.title: How bina tutoring is covered
items: bina's live online classes are invoiced as part-time tutoring, which can be taught online.
Part-time tutoring is capped at 720 hours a year for grades K–3 and 900 hours a year for grades 4–12.
You can request reimbursement for tutoring prepaid up to four months ahead.
SUFS reviews every request under state rules. Whether a request is approved, how much is repaid and when is decided by the state, not by bina.

faq.a: Florida students with a qualifying unique ability, shown by an IEP or a diagnosis from a licensed professional. There's no income limit.

faq.q: When is the deadline?

faq.a: Up to 60 days after all documents are in. 2026–27 funds can be spent until June 30, 2027, and requests must be submitted by July 31, 2027.

faq.q: Will someone help me with the application?

faq.q: Is bina responsible for this program?
faq.a: FES-UA is run by the state of Florida and managed by Step Up For Students, not by bina. Program amounts, eligibility, deadlines and reimbursement decisions are subject to change. Always confirm with the official program site before you rely on a number here.

faq.q: What is an ESA?
faq.a: An Education Savings Account is money your state puts aside for your child's education. You can spend it on approved expenses, including tuition at an approved school like bina.

faq.q: Which states can I use at bina?
faq.a: Arizona, New Hampshire, Idaho, Utah, West Virginia and Wyoming. Choose your state above for the details.

faq.q: Does the award cover all of bina's tuition?
faq.a: It covers a large part of it, and you top up the rest each month. Awards depend on your state and your family, and our financial aid team will confirm your numbers.

faq.q: Who applies, me or bina?
faq.a: You apply to your state's program on its official website. We go through the application with you and send everything the state needs from bina.

faq.q: Will someone help me through the process?
faq.a: Yes. Our financial aid team guides you from your first question to your first payment.

faq.q: Can my child start before my ESA is approved?
faq.a: Yes. You can enroll and pay bina directly while your application is being reviewed, then switch to ESA funding once it's approved.

faq.q: Do you offer a sibling discount?
faq.a: Yes. Each additional child gets $1,500 off tuition.

faq.q: My state isn't listed yet. Can my child still join bina?
faq.a: Yes. Families in any state can join bina with direct tuition. Ask us about your state, and we'll let you know what's possible.

faq.q: Is bina responsible for these programs?
faq.a: Each ESA program is run by its own state, not by bina. Amounts, eligibility and deadlines are set by the state and can change. Always confirm with your state's official program site before you rely on a number here.
